questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A professor wants to survey his own students for research. Which vulnerability is most at issue?
questions.rationale: Institutional vulnerability affects people under formal authority (students, employees, prisoners); a third party should gather consent.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 4 Categories of vulnerability (PDF p. 132)
questions.quote: Prisoners, student-professor relationships, end employee-employer relationships are all examples.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A terminally ill patient joins a drug trial believing it is a miracle cure. This reflects which vulnerability?
questions.rationale: Medical vulnerability: illness makes it hard to decide; the patient may see research as a cure.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 4 Categories of vulnerability (PDF p. 132)
questions.quote: the patient may perceive the research study as a miracle cure for their ailment

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A low-income volunteer is offered a very large payment to join a risky study. The REC would consider this:
questions.rationale: Payment that induces someone to accept risks they normally would not is unethical (economic vulnerability).
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 4 Economic vulnerability (PDF p. 132)
questions.quote: Paying a low-income volunteer a big quantity of money to participate in a risky surgery, for example, would be unethical.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A child is invited into a study and his parent consents. What else should the researcher do?
questions.rationale: A surrogate consents for those lacking capacity, but the person should still be included in the consent process.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 4 Cognitive vulnerability (PDF p. 132)
questions.quote: it is still necessary to inciude them in the consent process regardless of their capacity

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Within how many hours must a serious adverse event in a study be reported to the REC?
questions.rationale: SAEs are reported to the REC within 24 hours of discovery, with a report within 14 days.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 4 Summary and takeaways (PDF p. 134)
questions.quote: All significant adverse events (SAEs) must be reported to the REC within 24 hours of discovery

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: In student-initiated research, who must provide compensation for research-related injury?
questions.rationale: In investigator-initiated or student research, the investigator/institution is the sponsor and covers research-related injury.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 4 Summary and takeaways (PDF p. 134)
questions.quote: the investigator/institution conducting the study becomes the sponsor and is responsible for providing compensation

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A nurse notices a coworker lacks the skill for a procedure. What is the ethical action?
options: Report it to the nurse manager
questions.rationale: Inadequate competency is an ethical issue; the nurse informs the manager so training can be provided.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 4 Inadequate competencies (PDF p. 135)
questions.quote: Nurses who recognize a coworker's lack of knowledge are faced with the ethical dilemma of whether or not to inform their nurse manager.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A patient offers his nurse an expensive gift and asks for her phone number. This is an issue of:
questions.rationale: Nurses set boundaries: patients should not rely unduly on nurses, form sexual ties or give gifts.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 4 Setting professional boundaries (PDF p. 135)
questions.quote: Patients should not place undue reliance on nurses, nor should they form sexual ties with them or give them presents.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Shared decision-making mainly enhances the patient's:
questions.rationale: Shared decision-making lets patients and providers decide together, increasing autonomy and trust.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 4 Shared decision-making (PDF p. 136)
questions.quote: Shared patient decision-making increases patient autonomy

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which documentation practice follows the 'completeness' standard?
questions.rationale: Completeness means no spaces left between entries and documentation done on time with complete data.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 5 The 5Cs (PDF p. 141)
questions.quote: Make sure not to leave space between entries to record delayed entries.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which nursing note is best?
questions.rationale: Notes must be factual and meaningful, avoiding phrases like 'slept well' or 'usual day' and personal judgments.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 5 Guiding principle 1 (PDF p. 146)
questions.quote: avoids meaningless phrases such as 'slept well or 'usual day

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A nurse forgot to chart a medication given 2 hours ago. She should:
questions.rationale: Late entries are recorded as soon as possible, prefaced with date and time; records stay chronological and non-erasable.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 5 Guiding principle 1 (PDF p. 146)
questions.quote: chronological record of care (late entries recorded as soon as possible as to rectify the absence)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which abbreviations may a nurse use in the chart?
questions.rationale: Avoid abbreviations other than those approved in organizational policy by the Medical Records Department.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 5 Guiding principle 1 (PDF p. 146)
questions.quote: avoid use of abbreviations (other than those approved and documented in organizational policy

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A nurse falsifies vital signs she did not take. A regulatory authority would deem this:
questions.rationale: Falsifying or giving inaccurate documentation may be deemed unprofessional by a regulatory authority.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 5 Legislative requirements (PDF p. 143)
questions.quote: falsifying documentation, providing incomplete or inaccurate documentation

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Using charts in audits and accreditation reviews serves which purpose of documentation?
questions.rationale: Documentation is used in performance reviews, audits, accreditation and critical incident reviews.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 5 Purposes of documentation (PDF p. 143)
questions.quote: Documentation can be used to assess professional practice as part of quality assurance procedures

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which practice protects electronic health records?
options: Log off when leaving the terminal
questions.rationale: Fully log off, keep passwords private and hard to guess, and never delete information.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 5 Electronic documentation (PDF p. 148)
questions.quote: fully logging off when not using the system or when leaving a terminal

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: How should old patient census sheets be disposed of?
questions.rationale: Documents are destroyed in a way that keeps confidentiality, e.g., shredding or confidential bins.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 5 Guiding principle 3 (PDF p. 148)
questions.quote: disposing of documentation (where appropriate to destroy) in a manner which maintains confidentiality (eg confidential bins /shredding)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Advice given to a patient by telephone should be:
questions.rationale: Documentation includes interventions via telephone, with information obtained and advice given.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 5 Guiding principle 2 (PDF p. 147)
questions.quote: documentation of intervention via telephone ( including information obtained and advice given)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A psychiatric nursing note should be based on:
questions.rationale: Documentation is based on professional observation and assessment, without unfounded conclusions or personal judgments.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 5 Guiding principle 2 (PDF p. 147)
questions.quote: based on professional observation and assessment that does not have any basis in unfounded conclusions of personal judgements

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which requirement of ethical decision-making is the desire to do right regardless of cost?
questions.rationale: Ethical decisions require commitment (desire to do right), consciousness (consistency) and competency (skill to evaluate).
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Moral decision-making (PDF p. 153)
questions.quote: Commitment: The desire to do the right thing regardless of the cost

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An ethical nurse leader is best described as one who:
questions.rationale: Ethical leaders role-model ethics, create an ethical climate, and enforce sanctions for unethical conduct.
questions.source: Udan, Healthcare Ethics (2023), Ch. 6 Introduction (PDF p. 151)
questions.quote: They serve as role models of ethical behaviour.
